---
title: "Topic Selection & Presentation Scheduling"
---

The course project is an opportunity to investigate a topic in Monte Carlo or
quasi-Monte Carlo methods and communicate its value clearly and critically.
Approach the presentation as a report to colleagues who need to decide whether
the article, method, or software feature is worth pursuing further.

## Project types

Choose one of the following project types.

- **Research article review:** Review a scholarly research article related to
  Monte Carlo methods or their applications. This is an individual project,
  and each student must choose a different article. The topic should not
  substantially duplicate material discussed in class. In general, the
  article should have been published less than fifteen years ago.
- **QMCPy feature:** Create a new feature for `qmcpy` and a blog post that
  illustrates it. This project may be completed individually or by a team of
  two. Discuss the proposed feature with the instructor to ensure that its
  scope is appropriate.

## Topic selection and approval

1. Choose a project type and identify a focused topic.
2. Submit the topic for approval. Revised topics will use the same process.
3. Check the approved-topic list after submissions have been reviewed and
   revise the proposal if requested.

| Topic-selection item | Fall 2026 information |
|---|---|
| Topic submission deadline | **Friday, September 18** |
| Topic submission form | [Submit the Fall 2026 Project Selection form](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=PmWQ2gIeCEK2imIkiRvqYx5C7GZcajFJvSlbTido5G1UQjJTS0VFUE5VRlJLNUpDUDFMM1VER0FDSS4u) |
| Approved-topic list | **TBA** |

For an article review, identify the main idea, illustrate it with examples of
your own, offer warranted criticism, and suggest future work. For a QMCPy
feature, explain the need for the feature, demonstrate its use, and discuss
its strengths, limitations, and possible extensions.

## Presentation expectations

- Prepare a **15-minute oral presentation** followed by **5 minutes for
  questions and answers**.
- A two-person QMCPy feature team will have **30 minutes for the presentation**
  followed by **10 minutes for questions and answers**.
- Prepare a handout for the audience.
- Provide enough background for classmates who are not specialists in the
  exact topic, while remaining responsible for the technical details.
- Explain both strengths and weaknesses, including important assumptions and
  limitations.
- Be prepared to answer probing questions. Assessment depends on both the
  clarity of the presentation and the quality of the answers.

Detailed feedback questions and assessment guidance are on the
[Project Assessment](project-assessment.qmd) page.

Each student is expected to observe and assess **two** other presentations.
Arrive on time for both presentations and observations, be prepared, and give
substantive feedback. The final observation and submission procedures will be
posted when the schedule is available.

Presentations will be conducted like colloquium or conference talks. Arrive
early enough to set up without delaying the schedule. The instructor will
introduce each speaker, give time warnings, end the presentation when its
allotted time expires, and chair the question period. At the end of the talk,
conclude with “Thank you” or a similar closing and allow the chair to invite
questions.

## Presentation guidance

- Keep the big picture in view rather than getting bogged down in details.
- Motivate the topic with relevant background, prior work, or applications.
- Use a simple example to illuminate the main point.
- Discuss strengths, weaknesses, alternatives, and possible future work.
- Use clear plots, tables, pictures, and key formulas where they help the
  audience.
- Use your own words and give appropriate credit; do not plagiarize.
- Aim for roughly one slide per minute and avoid overloading slides.
- Dress business casual unless the final session instructions say otherwise.
- Look at the audience rather than reading notes.
- Practice beforehand, obtain feedback, and stay within the allotted time.
- Bring the laptop and adapters needed for the presentation, test the display
  connection in advance, and bring at least three copies of any handout.
- Review the [Project Assessment](project-assessment.qmd) questions while
  preparing the presentation.

Additional room-specific and session procedures will be added when the Fall
2026 presentation logistics are known.
